text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT DETECTED — spike in cudaIllegalMemoryAccess errors across serving-runtime-pool-a (3 nodes). Alerting oncall.
alex: seeing repeated container crashes on nodes gpu-a-11/12/13. crash loop with SIGSEGV in nvpeer. Suspect misaligned device address after recent model hot-reload. Logs attached below.
jamie: I can join. Is there customer impact? Any traffic routed there still?
emily: ~10% request errors for customers in us-west-2, some 5xxs. No broad outages but sustained error rate > SLO for embeddings route.
priya: starting triage: can someone paste the kernel oops and container backtrace? I want to see if it's a kernel-side pagewalk or userspace misaligned access.
alex: paste logs:
```
[2026-03-15T02:31:12Z] serving-runtime[gpu-a-11]: cuda: illegal memory access at 0x7f8a3f000000
[2026-03-15T02:31:12Z] containerd: task serving-process died: signal: 11
[2026-03-15T02:31:12Z] kworker/3:0: pagewalk: TLB invalid entry, VA 0x7ffd1a3e2000, PFN 0xffffffff
[2026-03-15T02:31:12Z] kernel: BUG: unable to handle kernel paging request at address 7f8a3f000000
```
alex: and userspace backtrace from our crash handler:
```
#0  0x7f8a3f00 in __nv_peer_access_helper+0x34
#1  0x7f8a3f90 in gpu_mem_copy+0x58
#2  0x55aab2 in serving::Loader::load_weights
#3  0x55bb0f in main
```
ron: interestingly, all three nodes had a PCIe hotplug event ~90s before the first crash (host logs show GPU rescan). Could be driver state corruption after hotplug.
jamie: if hotplug correlated, might be SMMU pagewalk entries getting stale — misaligned or stale device mappings.
emily: customer impact list: small set of embeddings customers + 2 managed customers experiencing retries. CS notified for two high-priority users.
priya: immediate plan: 1) remove traffic from affected nodes, 2) cordon and drain to evict pods gracefully, 3) if stable, perform node reboot or kernel module reload, 4) if reproduces, rollback recent model/runtime rollout.
ops-bot: runbook check: cordon + drain command recommended. /runbook/serving/hotplug-oom
alex: executing:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-a-11
kubectl drain gpu-a-11 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
``` 
alex: drain started on gpu-a-11. Pod evictions show some pods stuck in terminating due to open NVML handles.
jamie: try forced kill of stuck containers after 30s: `crictl rm -f <id>`
infra-bot: note: drain will trigger fallback routing to regional spare capacity; latency may spike.
priya: while we drain, gather a vmcore and nvcrash logs from one crashed node. Use this:
```
sudo abrtd-collect --nvlog /var/log/nvidia/gpu-a-11/nvcrash.log --save /tmp/crash-collect.tar.gz
```
alex: collected crash bundle and uploaded to s3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/3523456789/gpu-a-11-bundle.tar.gz
alex: initial kernel trace suggests a pagewalk race; I see entries like:
```
[  123.456789] dma_map: mapped device address 0x7f8a3f000000 -> pfn 0x0 (invalid)
[  123.456790] pagewalk: received misaligned pte while walking for device 0000:65:00.0
```
ron: can we repro in non-prod? If hotplug is the trigger, reproduce steps: 1) live hot-unplug GPU, 2) rescan, 3) run stress workload with frequent KV cache and long sequence lengths.
jamie: agree. Priya, what's your read on rollback? We rolled a runtime patch last night to change KV cache eviction whoops.
priya: rollback candidate: runtime v3.4.2 -> v3.4.1. 3.4.2 introduced new async page prefault path. If draining doesn't stabilize, prepare canary rollback to a single node group.
emily: customer comms: sending interim blurb: "We're investigating increased 5xx errors in US-WEST affecting embeddings. We're routing requests off impacted capacity and expect mitigation within 30-60 minutes. We'll follow up with root cause." 
alex: after cordon/drain of gpu-a-11/12, crash rate dropped by ~70% but two nodes still showing sporadic illegal access (gpu-a-13 and gpu-b-05). Redirecting traffic away from pool-a entirely.
ops-bot: routing policy updated: shift embeddings traffic to dedicated fallback pool-b until further notice.
ron: rebooted gpu-a-12 and reloaded nvidia kernel module on gpu-a-13. Post-reboot, nvlink topology consistent and no immediate crashes for 8 minutes.
priya: we should also disable the new async prefetch via env var `RW_DISABLE_ASYNC_PREFETCH=1` for the runtime process; deploy as a hotfix to affected nodes. That avoids the new pagewalk path.
alex: applying hotfix to a canary pod now: `kubectl set env deployment/serving-runtime RW_DISABLE_ASYNC_PREFETCH=1 -n prod --selector=pool=pool-a --record` (canary applied to single node first)
jamie: monitor memory and GPU pagewalk counters. Add a temporary tracepoint for `mmu_notifier` in kernel to capture if mappings are invalidated during device access.
infra-bot: set up ephemeral perf trace on gpu-a-13, collecting mmu events to s3.
emily: CS update: added note to affected customers that we're performing targeted reboots and a config hotfix; asked to escalate if customer sees persistent errors.
alex: canary runtime with env var seems stable for ~12m, no new illegal access on that pod. Rolling 3 more pods with the env var.
priya: still want full postmortem: items to collect: crash bundles, kernel oops, pci hotplug events, nv driver version, runtime version, model reload timeline, recent commits to async prefetch. Tagging for research/eng-ml and eng-runtime.
jamie: if we confirm it's a race between hotplug and async prefetch pagewalk, long-term fix options: 1) serialize hotplug handling with driver quiesce, 2) add device mapping validation in prefetch path, 3) kernel patch to avoid misaligned PTE acceptance.
ron: any need for customer credits? If SLO breached for >1hr we'll trigger compensation playbook. ETA to full recovery?
emily: routing off pool-a and hotfix rollouts, estimated 45-90min to full restore depending on reboots and validation.
ops-bot: reminder: follow incident severity timeline. Assigning Sev2 until error rate below SLO for 30m.
alex: will keep thread updated. Next steps: continue rollouts, collect remaining crash bundles, start repro in staging with controlled hotplug events.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED — severity: SEV2, assigned: oncall (alex), escalation: eng-runtime (priya), eng-ml (ron)."
